notes:
Scope: civilians outside the garrison at Chicago on 14 Aug 1812. Status values are present / probably_present / absent / dead_before, plus "unknown" where no source decides; absent people are listed under excluded.

Totals: Helm's narrative (Quaife app. VI) gives "14 Citizens 15 children and 9 women" at the evacuation. Kirkland says the whole civilian body was "probably about thirty". Quaife (ch. X) says the twelve militia were all the able-bodied civilian men. Only Burns, Cooper and (conjecturally) Lee, the Lee son, Fettle and LeClaire are named, so about six militiamen stay anonymous. Do not invent names for them.

Locations on 14 Aug: Kinzie's family was inside the fort (Andreas p. 74; Wau-Bun ch. XVIII). The other civilian families had fortified the former agency house after April (Quaife ch. X lines 8633-8636; Wau-Bun ch. XVIII lines 5790-5792): first_fort_outer_agents_house, graded inferred for 14 Aug. The Ouilmette household stayed in its own house.

Conflicts:
(1) Ouilmette's house: Andreas p. 92 says "just north" of Kinzie's; Currey says "close in the rear" (PG 52346 lines 693-694); Kirkland says "Just west" (PG 59624 line 2904). The repo's ouilmette_house_1812 follows the draught/Cooper reading, the easternmost of three houses west of Kinzie. Flag this for review.
(2) Burns's given name: Thomas (Quaife, from Griffith's 1820 letter), John (Kirkland, Currey), Jos. (Heald's list in the Helm narrative). Prefer Thomas.
(3) Mrs. Burns's death: about 1823 (Edwards via Wentworth, Quaife) or about 1832 (Edwards letter, Kirkland app. G).
(4) Cooper: Quaife makes Joseph/James Cooper Mrs. Burns's son; Edwards (Kirkland app. G) makes the killed Cooper Isabella's father.
(5) Josette LaFramboise married Beaubien in 1812 (Andreas p. 84) or 1814 (Quaife).
(6) The Lee house: on the lake shore (Wau-Bun), at the river mouth (Currey), or southwest of the fort (Quaife).
(7) Wells arrived on 12 Aug (Helm), 13 Aug (Heald, Quaife ch. X line 8908) or 14 Aug (Wau-Bun ch. XVIII lines 6032-6034). Winnemeg's arrival is given as 7, 8 or 9 Aug. Notes only: the Miami men are another researcher's scope.

Source weight: Quaife (ch. XI fn 631) judges Wau-Bun's rescue stories largely literary. The Helm concealment and Black Jim's axe rest on Wau-Bun alone. Andreas and Hurlbut quotes come from Internet Archive OCR, cleaned of OCR noise and matched fuzzily against the OCR text; checking the page scan is recommended before display.

Helm's "Captain Heald through Kenzie sending his two Negroes" (Quaife app. VI) is ambiguous and is not used to identify Kinzie servants. No source read calls any Kinzie servant enslaved in 1812. Nash's 1804 indenture is the only documented unfree status, and Nash was not at Chicago.

Wau-Bun quotes are from the 1856 text as reprinted in PG 51737 (1901 Caxton Club edition). No Thwaites note is cited, so no new source is proposed.
